source_label: General explainer, draft, not yet reviewed by the technology office

entries.plain: What is new in your technical approach compared with anything previously made public in papers, talks, posters, theses, patents, or products.
entries.example: A passive acoustic array that isolates micro-crack attenuation shifts in concrete beams without lane closures, whereas published methods require active ultrasonic transducers.
entries.what_office_asks: Which specific step, mechanism, composition, or algorithm has not been described in prior public disclosures?
entries.source_label: General explainer, draft, not yet reviewed by the technology office

entries.plain: Any earlier publication, preprint, conference presentation, thesis, website, patent, or commercial product that describes closely related technology before a filing date.
entries.example: Your own earlier workshop abstract, a competitor's published journal paper, or an existing commercial sensor datasheet.
entries.what_office_asks: What are the closest papers, patents, or products (including your own prior work) that a patent examiner or licensee would compare against?
entries.source_label: General explainer, draft, not yet reviewed by the technology office

entries.plain: A legal standard based on who conceived the specific technical solution claimed in a patent, which differs from academic authorship on a manuscript.
entries.example: A co-author who ran standard testbench measurements or edited the manuscript without conceiving part of the technical solution may be an author on the paper without being listed as an inventor.
entries.what_office_asks: Who contributed to conceiving the technical concepts, and what specific part did each person conceive?
entries.source_label: General explainer, draft, not yet reviewed by the technology office

entries.plain: Any non-confidential communication that enables someone in the field to understand or reproduce the invention, such as a journal article, arXiv preprint, conference talk, poster, thesis defense, or public GitHub repository.
entries.example: Posting a manuscript on arXiv or presenting slides at an IEEE conference starts a one-year U.S. patent filing window and can immediately affect foreign patent rights.
entries.what_office_asks: When was the work first shared outside the university without a confidentiality agreement, or when is the next planned talk, poster, preprint, or publication?
entries.source_label: General explainer, draft, not yet reviewed by the technology office

entries.plain: How far the technology has progressed from an initial theoretical concept or lab observation to simulation, benchtop validation, prototype testing, or field deployment.
entries.example: A radar respiration monitor tested across 18 bench trials in a laboratory setting versus an unverified mathematical bound.
entries.what_office_asks: What experimental data, simulations, benchtop measurements, or prototype runs exist today, and what remains untested?
entries.source_label: General explainer, draft, not yet reviewed by the technology office

entries.plain: How clearly a research result defines a real-world problem, a specific user or application context, measurable evidence, and differentiation from existing alternatives.
entries.example: Moving from observing an unexpected 14 dB acoustic shift in lab beams to specifying how bridge inspectors would deploy the sensor and what evidence still needs collection.
entries.what_office_asks: What problem does this solve, who would use it, how does it compare with current practice, and what experimental validation exists so far?
entries.source_label: General explainer, draft, not yet reviewed by the technology office

entries.plain: The concrete practical use case, workflow, product, or user group that benefits from the research result outside the laboratory.
entries.example: Emergency department nurses using a 15-minute saliva assay for rapid sepsis triage instead of waiting for central lab blood cultures.
entries.what_office_asks: Who is the specific user, operator, or buyer, and what changes in their workflow or cost structure?
entries.source_label: General explainer, draft, not yet reviewed by the technology office

entries.plain: How your technical method or design differs in mechanism, performance, cost, or workflow from current practice and competing commercial or academic approaches.
entries.example: Reducing ammonia synthesis pressure by 35% in continuous pilot runs compared with conventional high-pressure Haber-Bosch reactors.
entries.what_office_asks: What do practitioners use today, and what measurable advantage or trade-off does your approach show over those alternatives?
entries.source_label: General explainer, draft, not yet reviewed by the technology office

entries.plain: A situation in which an employee's outside financial interest, consulting arrangement, equity holding, or external role could influence, or reasonably appear to influence, their university teaching, research, or administrative responsibilities.
entries.example: Holding founder equity or a paid advisory board role in a startup that sponsors research in your university lab or employs your graduate advisees.
entries.what_office_asks: Do any contributors hold outside consulting agreements, equity, or leadership roles in an entity related to this research or its funding?
entries.source_label: General explainer, draft, not yet reviewed by the technology office

entries.plain: A confidential internal document (UM-16C at the University of Missouri System) submitted to the technology transfer office to report a new research discovery or technical creation before public release or commercialization.
entries.example: Submitting the UM-16C form to the UMKC Office of Research Services / Technology Commercialization before presenting a conference paper or releasing software.
entries.what_office_asks: Have you described the technical problem, novel aspects, funding sources, contributors, prior art, and any past or upcoming public disclosures?
entries.source_label: General explainer, draft, not yet reviewed by the technology office

entries.plain: A formal agreement in which the university grants a company or organization permission to make, use, or sell university-owned intellectual property under specified financial and diligence terms without transferring underlying ownership.
entries.example: Granting an established medical device manufacturer or a faculty startup a right to commercialize a university-patented sensor or curated clinical dataset.
entries.what_office_asks: Which companies or industry sectors might licence this technology, and are there existing sponsor or third-party agreements that affect licensing rights?
entries.source_label: General explainer, draft, not yet reviewed by the technology office

entries.plain: Ownership shares, stock, stock options, or other ownership interests in an outside business entity such as a faculty spinout or industry sponsor.
entries.example: Holding founder shares in an SBIR partner startup that seeks to licence university technology or sponsor laboratory testing.
entries.what_office_asks: Does any investigator or family member hold ownership shares or options in a company connected to the research, sponsorship, or potential licensing?
entries.source_label: General explainer, draft, not yet reviewed by the technology office
